This is Mika, in Ishinomaki. At six forty-one, her biggest problem was the toaster.
At six forty-two, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake. Her phone already had a statement ready.
Three minutes later: a tsunami warning, plus a note about her insurance.
Mika walked to higher ground. Her phone offered an upgrade.
At the shelter, the power went out. Her phone suggested candles. Premium ones.
Day two: rescue teams from the United States, and a six-hundred-page form.
That evening, another aftershock. Mika reached page two hundred.
Day four: the trains came back, and so did Mika. The toast was waiting.
